title: Preimage of a singleton under hard-sample dualization
statement: Fix a positive integer $n$, and let $D$ denote the dualization map on the finite space of hard samples, which sends a hard sample to the one obtained by exchanging Alice's and Bob's bits and reversing the order of the coordinates. Then for every hard sample $\omega$, the preimage of the singleton $\{\omega\}$ under $D$ is exactly the singleton $\{D(\omega)\}$; that is, $D^{-1}(\{\omega\}) = \{D(\omega)\}$.
replaced: The preimage of a singleton under hard-sample duality is the dual singleton.
